text.p: Mitchell Energy & Development Corp said it has completed the sale of its real estate unit Woodlands Corp for $543 million and would pay $10 million more in state taxes on the transaction.

The natural gas producer said it would take a $65 million to $70 million after-tax charge in the second quarter ended July 31 for the sale. That's $10 million more than the $55 million to $60 million after-tax loss the company expected to post when it first announced the sale June 12.
"Completing the work, we became aware of additional state taxes owed on the property," a spokeswoman said Friday. She added Mitchell will report its second-quarter earnings September 10.

Mitchell said it expected to net $460 million after income taxes and transaction costs from Woodland's buyers, a partnership of Crescent Real Estate Equities Co and Morgan Stanley Real Estate Fund II LP.

Crescent said Thursday in a separate statement it will serve as Woodlands' general partner and hold a partnership interest of 42.5 percent, while the Morgan Stanley Dean Witter Discover & Co fund will hold a 57.5 percent stake.

Crescent said a combined $369 million revolving credit facility and term loan led by BankBoston Corp and Morgan Stanley Senior Funding partially financed the $543 million price tag of the 27,000-acre development north of Houston.

A Crescent spokesman said Friday Crescent Operating Inc will buy for $1 million all of the voting stock in a newly-created company that will hold a 42.5 percent proportionate interest in Woodlands' residential (20,000 single family homes) and commercial land (2,900 acres) assets.

Crescent Real Estate shares its chairman and chief executive with Crescent Operating, but the companies have separate boards, ownership, legal structures, and are both publicly traded, the spokesman added.
The spokesman said said the voting stock represented a five percent equity stake in new company, while Crescent Real Estate will keep a 95 percent interest.
